subject: Surge readiness metrics — measurement protocol & acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@globalbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Surge readiness metrics — measurement protocol & acceptance criteria

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is a draft measurement protocol that we propose to use to validate surge readiness for your real-time document-parsing endpoint. The attachment (surge-test-plan-draft.xlsx) contains the step-by-step harness configuration, target workload profiles, sampling windows, and acceptance checks. High-level acceptance criteria we propose: 

- Sustained throughput: maintain target qps ±5% over a 15-minute window (we recommend target windows at 100, 500, 2k qps).
- P99 latency: <= 800 ms for steady-state sustained windows.
- Microburst tail (2–30s bursts): P99 <= 1,200 ms, P995 <= 2,000 ms.
- Cold-start recovery: 90% of endpoints recover to steady-state P95 within 60s after instance restart.
- Prefix/KV cache hit-rate: >= 85% after warmup; we capture warmup curve and time-to-85%.
- Quality guardrails: end-to-end output pass-rate on your evaluation set >= 98% (we'll run evaluation payloads in parallel).

Measurement notes and instrumentation: we will provide an isolated test harness that can replay representative traffic mixes (exact payloads we discussed), drive multi-region fanout if needed, and inject auth headers you provide. Instrumentation will emit per-request trace ids so you can reconcile with your observability. We also measure internal metrics like batching efficiency, KV cache warmup, and backpressure events (queue depth, retry loops).

Questions for you to confirm:
1) Do you want multi-region failover exercised during the same run or in a separate test?
2) Any procurement constraints for firing load from our hosted test agent (billing/temporary infra)?
3) Confirm the sample workload window you want us to use for acceptance (we suggested the three windows above).

Next steps: if this looks good we can schedule a 2-hour dry run and then a 4-hour acceptance run. The dry run will capture baseline metrics and confirm hooks to your syslog/trace collectors. I copied Ben and Kimberly to align on logistics and instrumentation.

Attachments: surge-test-plan-draft.xlsx, synthetic-workload-samples.csv

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@globalbank.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-security@globalbank.com, procurement@globalbank.com
Date: 2026-09-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Surge readiness metrics — measurement protocol & acceptance criteria

Evelyn,

Thanks for the draft — useful level of detail. A few clarifying items before we lock dates: 

- Multi-region: we'd prefer the acceptance run to include a failover exercise (primary region east-us, fail to eu-west) as part of the same weekend run if feasible. That helps validate routing and cache-warmup across regions.
- Auth: ops-security wants the test harness to use a short-lived test token; can you confirm you support injecting the token and honoring our IP allowlist?
- Billing: procurement asked whether test-related infra (if you spin up additional runners) is billable or included as a one-off credit. Please include proposed commercial treatment.
- Data handling: confirm that logs and traces generated during the test will be retained for 30 days and then purged unless we request archiving. ops-security is particularly focused on PII elimination in logs.

We'd like a firm run window next Friday morning (2026-09-25) but can shift if your team needs more time.

-Michael
Michael Torres
Director, Platform Ops — GlobalBank

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-18T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Surge readiness metrics — measurement protocol & acceptance criteria

Eve/Kim/Marissa —

Saw Michael's asks. Quick internal plan:
- Kimberly, can you confirm multi-region failover steps and whether our runner will simulate cross-region cold starts (cache flush + cross-region SNI)? Also confirm token injection support and IP allowlist flow.
- Marissa, procurement will want explicit language about credits for test infra. Can you draft a one-off credit clause (e.g., up to $X for test infra, applied as credit on the first invoice) and share with procurement?
- Evelyn, I'll draft the reply to Michael consolidating the answers; once Kim confirms instrumentation language I'll add a short annex describing log retention and PII redaction.

Proposed commercial note: offer a single test-credit for infrastructure for this acceptance run (one-time, non-recurring). That reduces procurement friction and is a common signal.

Attaching a small sample workload CSV that we can present to GlobalBank if they want payload-level visibility: synthetic-workload-samples.csv

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-19T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Surge readiness metrics — measurement protocol & acceptance criteria

Ben/Eve —

Technical confirmation / clarifications:
- Multi-region failover: yes, we can exercise a primary->secondary failover during the same run. Our harness supports staged DNS failover + explicit connection drain to emulate client rebind. We will capture region-to-region KV-cache warmup curves and annotate metrics with region tags. Expect an additional 12–18% transient latency inflation during network failover windows; we'll include rollback thresholds.
- Token injection & allowlist: supported. We will accept a short-lived HMAC bearer token; our runner will present it on every request. Please provide the IP allowlist CIDRs for our runner to use.
- Instrumentation & sampling: we compute both edge-observed latency and internal service processing latency. For tail quantiles we use contiguous 1s micro-windows and compute P95/P99/P995 across those windows to avoid inflation from long idle spans. We also capture: batch-size distribution, KV cache hit-rate per-prefix, queue depth histograms, and backpressure event counts. The measurement-instrumentation.md attachment explains exact metric names and units.
- Data handling: logs/traces produced in your environment (we will not ship PII to Redwood unless explicitly requested). By default we will store test traces in a tenant-scoped bucket for 30 days. We will support a one-time export if you request archiving.

I'll run a 30-minute lab locally and share a short run-snapshot (json + sample traces) before we do the dry run.

Kimberly Park
Principal Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@globalbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ops-security@globalbank.com, procurement@globalbank.com
Date: 2026-09-22T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Surge readiness metrics — measurement protocol & acceptance criteria

Michael —

Thanks for the quick review and for surfacing ops and procurement requirements. Per our internal alignment (Kimberly and Ben above) here's the consolidated plan and answers to your questions: 

1) Multi-region failover: we will include a primary->secondary failover during the acceptance run. The plan will intentionally schedule the failover in the second hour of the 4-hour acceptance window to allow warmup and baseline capture. We will annotate region tags on all metrics and provide a warmup curve for KV hit-rate.

2) Token & allowlist: our harness supports short-lived HMAC bearer tokens; we will use the token you provide. Please share the CIDRs for your allowlist.

3) Billing for test infra: Redwood will absorb test-run runner costs for this single acceptance event as a one-time credit. We will reflect that in the commercial note and in the statement of work: "One-time test-infrastructure credit applied to first invoice for acceptance run GLB-2026-045." Marissa will follow up with a short statement for procurement.

4) Data handling and retention: by default logs and traces from this run will be retained for 30 days in tenant-scoped storage and then purged. We will not persist any PII unless you explicitly request archival and provide approved S3 location/controls. ops-security, feel free to propose any additional constraints and we will incorporate them into the annex.

Proposed schedule: dry run Friday 2026-09-25 08:00–10:00 PT; acceptance run Sunday 2026-09-27 02:00–06:00 PT (to minimize production impact). If those windows don't work, propose alternatives.

Attachments: surge-test-plan-redwood-final.xlsx (final test plan), measurement-instrumentation.md

Next steps: 1) Michael to confirm windows and provide allowlist CIDRs + short-lived test token; 2) procurement to confirm credit language from Marissa; 3) Kimberly will circulate a 30-minute run-snapshot before the dry run.

Looking forward —
Evelyn Hart
Principal Solutions Architect
